attributes.body_ja:
「たって」は「ても」や「でも」の砕（くだ）けた表現（ひょうげん）です。「ても」や「でも」と同（おな）じように「もし (A) でも」や「(A) だとしても」といった意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。

動詞（どうし）と使（つか）われる場合（ばあい）、「たって」の「た」は動詞（どうし）の過去形（かこけい）の「た」になります。

イ形容詞（けいようし）と使（つか）われる場合（ばあい）、イ形容詞（けいようし）のク形（けい）が「たって」と結（むす）びつきます。

名詞（めいし）とナ形容詞（けいようし）と使（つか）われる場合（ばあい）、「た」は「だ」と濁（にご）り、「だって」という形（かたち）が名詞（めいし）やナ形容詞（けいようし）の語幹（ごかん）と結（むす）びつきます。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「たって」は「ても」の砕（くだ）けた形（かたち）として使（つか）われていますが、もともとは助動詞（じょどうし）「た」と助詞（じょし）の「とて」を組（く）み合（あ）わせた「たとて」という言葉（ことば）から来（き）ています。「とて」は古（ふる）い表現（ひょうげん）で、「と言（い）っても」を短縮（たんしゅく）した形（かたち）だと考（かんが）えられています。そのため、現代（げんだい）日本語（にほんご）の短縮形（たんしゅくけい）「たって」にも「たと言（い）っても」のニュアンスが残（のこ）っています。
attributes.body:
たって is a casual structure that carries the same meaning as 'ても' or 'でも', and can be used with a wide variety of words. Common translations include 'even if (A)', 'even though (A)', or 'no matter how (A)'.

In the case of verbs, たって conjugates in the standard way that the た past-tense form usually would.

For い-Adjectives, たって attaches to the conjugative く-form.

For nouns and な-Adjectives, た will change to だ, and だって will then be used with the stem noun or adjective.

Fun-fact

Although たって is widely considered a casual form of ても, it originally stems from たとて, which is a combination of the auxiliary verb た, and the particle とて, which itself is thought to be an old-fashioned abbreviation of と言（い）っても. In this way, the modern abbreviation of たって still reflects the original extended nuance of たと言（い）っても 'even if (A) is said, (B)'.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.description: ったって and たって

attributes.body: ても and たって both mean 'even if' or 'even though,' with the main difference being tone and formality. ても is widely used in both everyday speech and writing, while たって is more casual and emphatic, typically found in informal conversation. Aside from tone, their meaning is nearly identical, e.g., 行っても and 行ったって both mean 'Even if I/you/etc. go...'

second_relatable.title: たって
second_relatable.meaning: Even if, Even though, No matter how

attributes.body: ては often marks a condition with a negative or cautionary result, as in 無駄遣いしては貯金できない (If you waste money, you can’t save). たって means even if or no matter, used casually like ても but with a rougher tone, as in 誰に聞いたって分からない (Even if you ask anyone, they won’t know).

second_relatable.title: たって
second_relatable.meaning: Even if, Even though, No matter how

attributes.body: These are two expressions that can look very similar, or even identical in some cases, as たって when used with nouns will become だって. As an overall guideline, だって is a casual expression used to express 'I hear (A)' or 'they say (A)', or as a colloquial 'because', while たって is one way to say 'even though (A)' or 'even (A)', similar to ても or でも.

first_relatable.title: だって
first_relatable.meaning: I heard/was said, Because, But, Even or also, Even if or even though

second_relatable.title: たって
second_relatable.meaning: Even if, Even though, No matter how

attributes.body: にしても and たって are related in that たって is a more casual form of ても, meaning 'even if'. にしても could be rephrased as にしたって, which sounds more informal and emotional. For example, どこに行くにしても ('No matter where you go') can also be expressed as どこ行くにしたって.

first_relatable.title: にしても
first_relatable.meaning: Even though, Even if, Even when, Also

second_relatable.title: たって
second_relatable.meaning: Even if, Even though, No matter how

attributes.body: Both express contrastive conditionals. たとえ〜ても is neutral or formal, e.g. たとえ雨に降られても気にしない 'Even if I get rained on, I won't care.' たって is casual and conversational, often used with emotional insistence, e.g. そんなこと言ったってしょうがないよ 'Even if you say that, there's nothing we can do.'

first_relatable.title: たとえ〜ても
first_relatable.meaning: Even if…is the case, Supposing that

second_relatable.title: たって
second_relatable.meaning: Even if, Even though, No matter how

attributes.body: どうしても and たって are similar in that both express ideas like 'even' or 'no matter', but they are used differently. どうしても appears at the beginning of a sentence to convey 'no matter what'. For example, どうしても勝ちたい ('I want to win no matter what'). たって is a casual verb ending that functions like ても. In fact, どうしても can be expressed more colloquially as どうしたって.

second_relatable.title: たって
second_relatable.meaning: Even if, Even though, No matter how

attributes.body: Both translate as even if, but differ in nuance. たって is a casual equivalent of ても, as in 雨が降ったって行く (I’ll go even if it rains). たところで appears in negative or futile contexts, as in 頑張ったところで無駄だ (Even if you try hard, it’s useless).

first_relatable.title: たって
first_relatable.meaning: Even if, Even though, No matter how

second_relatable.title: たところで
second_relatable.meaning: Even if ~ cannot or will not, Even though ~ not

attributes.body: Both show even if, but with different tone. たって is casual and conversational, equivalent to ても, as in 子どもだって分かる (Even a child would understand). ようが～まいが is formal and emphatic, often with contrasting options, as in 成功しようが失敗しようが挑戦する (Whether we succeed or fail, we’ll try).
